text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden-onset spinning vertigo lasting only 3 minutes, triggered by head movement (rolling over in bed), with full recovery and no auditory symptoms, is classic for BPPV. Gastroenteritis is incorrect given the specific vertigo characteristics.
